Name: NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)
Organization Info: leads the nation civilian space exploration, aeronautics research, and scientific discovery. NASA conducts robotic and human space missions, develops new aerospace technologies, studies Earth and planetary systems, and carries out astrophysics and heliophysics research.
Mission: Lead U.S. civil space exploration and research, Human and robotic spaceflight, Space science (planetary, astrophysics, heliophysics, Earth science), Aeronautics research and technology, Development and demonstration of new space technologies, International and commercial partnerships, Inspire and educate through STEM engagement, Support U.S. economic growth and innovation through technology transfer and industry collaboration
Subordinate Centers: Ames Research Center (CA), Armstrong Flight Research Center (CA), Glenn Research Center (OH), Goddard Space Flight Center (MD), Goddard Institute for Space Studies (NY), IV&V Facility (WV), Jet Propulsion Laboratory (CA, managed by Caltech), Johnson Space Center (TX), Kennedy Space Center (FL), Langley Research Center (VA), Marshall Space Flight Center (AL), Stennis Space Center (MS), Wallops Flight Facility (VA), White Sands Test Facility (NM)
Location: Mary W. Jackson NASA Headquarters, 300 E Street SW, Washington, D.C.

Name: USSF (United States Space Force)
Organization Info: organize, train, and equip space forces to protect U.S. and allied interests in space and to ensure freedom of operation in the space domain. The USSF manages military satellite communications, GPS systems, missile warning systems, and space domain awareness. It also plays a critical role in defending space assets from threats and advancing the strategic use of space for national security.
Mission: Space domain awareness, Missile warning and tracking, Satellite communications, Positioning, navigation, and timing (GPS/PNT), Space control and defense, Launch operations and assured access to space, Space-based ISR (intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance), Cyber and nuclear operations support, Acquisition and sustainment of space systems, Doctrine development and training of space professionals
Subordinate Centers: Space Operations Command (SpOC), Space Systems Command (SSC), Space Training and Readiness Command (STARCOM), Space Delta 5 (Combined Space Operations Center), Space Delta 15 (National Space Defense Center), and various Space Force Bases such as Peterson SFB, Schriever SFB, and Vandenberg SFB
Location: Pentagon, Arlington, Virginia and multiple bases

Name: DARPA (Defense Advanced Research Projects  Agency)
Organization Info: focuses on high-risk, high-reward research that can provide revolutionary advances in defense capabilities. The agency funds and oversees projects in areas like artificial intelligence, robotics, quantum computing, biotechnology, and space technologies. In the space sector, DARPA has initiated programs to improve satellite resilience, rapid launch capabilities, and the use of space for tactical and operational advantage.
Mission: Create technological surprise for U.S. national security, funds and manages high-risk and high-reward research and development projects, does not operate its own labs but works with academia, industry, and government partners to execute projects that often result in revolutionary military and dual-use technologies (e.g., ARPANET/Internet, stealth, GPS, drones, AI, mRNA vaccines).
Subordinate Centers: Biological Technologies Office (BTO), Defense Sciences Office (DSO), Information Innovation Office (I2O), Microsystems Technology Office (MTO), Strategic Technology Office (STO), and Tactical Technology Office (TTO)

Name: FAA AST(Office of Commercial Space Transportation)
Organization Info: responsible for regulating and promoting the commercial space transportation industry in the United States. The AST ensures public safety during commercial space launches and reentries, licenses launch and reentry operations, and oversees spaceport operations. Additionally, the office encourages innovation and investment in space transportation, supports the integration of commercial space activities into the national airspace, and works to streamline regulatory processes to foster a competitive commercial space market.
Mission: Regulate and license U.S. commercial space launch and reentry activities to ensure public safety, property protection, and national security/foreign policy interests, Encourage and promote commercial space launches and reentries by the private sector, Oversee safety inspections and investigations, Recommend changes in statutes, regulations, and policies, Facilitate the growth and strengthening of U.S. space transportation infrastructure, Integrate commercial space operations into the National Airspace System, Support research and development in commercial space transportation safety
Subordinate Centers: Office of Operational Safety, Office of Strategic Management, Office of Spaceports, Divisions for Licensing & Evaluation, Regulations & Analysis, Safety Inspection, Operations Integration, Innovation, Business Operations, Safety Authorization, and others
Location: 800 Independence Avenue SW, Suite 335, Washington, D.C.
